# Computer advanced searches

Jamf **Reports** for Macs are Classic **advanced computer searches**. Buddy lists and mutates the saved search definition (`criteria`, `display_fields`) and runs it for result rows. `get` / `computer_search` strip the embedded `computers` array so a definition load stays small; `results` / `computer_search_computers` returns those rows. There is no Pro JSON CRUD for this object.

## Agent rules

- Do not treat `computerreports` as a second resource noun — it is the results path for the same advanced-search IDs.
- Do not invent a Pro JSON catalog for advanced computer searches; there is none.
- Do not return `computers` from `computer_search` / `get` — use `computer_search_computers` / `results`.
- Do not conflate this with per-Mac Classic `computerhardwaresoftwarereports` / `computerapplicationusage`, fleet `computerapplications`, or Platform `ddm_*` / `benchmark_*` / `blueprint_status`.
- Do not add `buddy report`. Copy/migrate is not in this slice.

## Facts

- List: `computer_searches(filter?)` · `buddy computer-search list` — Classic `{id, name}`; client-side substring on id/name
- Load definition: `computer_search(id=…)` / `computer_search(name=…)` · `buddy computer-search get` / `get id <name>` — `computers` stripped
- Run / results: `computer_search_computers(id, filter?, fields?)` · `buddy computer-search results [--fields=…] [--csv] [--id]` — CSV uses spaced headers and omits id unless `--id`; `--fromjson`/`--flatten` for JSON-string cells
- Create: `computer_search_create(body)` · `create --file=` or `create <name>` — Classic JSON (`and_or` / `search_type`); POST `…/id/0`
- Replace: `computer_search_put(id, body)` · `put <search-id> --file=` — Full PUT; `computers` stripped before send
- Delete: `computer_search_delete(id=…)` / `ids=…` · `delete <search-id> […]` — One or more IDs
- Jamf’s Reports UI is this saved-search object, not DDM / benchmark / blueprint status reports.
- Definition CRUD is Classic `/JSSResource/advancedcomputersearches`. Result rows prefer Classic `/JSSResource/computerreports` for the same search ID, then fall back to the ACS `computers` array.
- Pass Jamf JSON through: Classic snake_case `and_or` / `search_type`. Criteria helpers like `smart_group_criteria` are not in this slice.

## Builtins

### computer_searches

List advanced computer searches

Returns: list of {id, name}

#### Parameters (JSON Schema)

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "properties": {
    "filter": {
      "description": "client-side substring on id/name",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "title": "computer_searches",
  "type": "object"
}
```

### computer_search

Returns: dict

#### Parameters (JSON Schema)

```json

  "type": "object"
}
```

### computer_search_computers

Run a saved search and return result rows

Returns: list of dict (display fields kept)

#### Parameters (JSON Schema)

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "properties": {
    "fields": {
      "description": "display-field names to keep (JSON keys or Computer Name)",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "filter": {
      "description": "client-side substring on any result field",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "id": {
      "description": "search-id",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "id"
  ],
  "title": "computer_search_computers",
  "type": "object"
}
```

## Examples

```python
def main():
    rows = computer_searches(filter="Chrome")
    if not rows:
        return []
    sid = rows[0]["id"]
    defn = computer_search(id=sid)
    comps = computer_search_computers(id=sid, filter="lab")
    return {"name": defn.get("name"), "matches": len(comps)}
```
